label: Systems of Linear Inequalities
overview: A system of linear inequalities is solved by finding the region of the coordinate plane that satisfies all inequalities simultaneously. SAT questions ask you to identify the correct feasible region on a graph, determine whether a given point satisfies the system, or match a graph to a system. The feasible region is always the overlap of the individual half-planes.

keyFormulas.name: To find the feasible region
keyFormulas.latex: \text{Shade each inequality separately; feasible region = overlap}

keyFormulas.name: Test a point
keyFormulas.latex: \text{Substitute a point into all inequalities; if ALL are satisfied, it is in the region}

workedExamples.problem: Which point satisfies both y ≤ 2x + 3 and y ≥ x − 1? Check (4, 2).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.content: (4, 2) fails the second inequality, so it is NOT in the feasible region.

commonMistakes.mistake: Only testing one of the two inequalities
commonMistakes.fix: A point must satisfy ALL inequalities in the system. Check every one.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shading the wrong side of a boundary line after rearranging
commonMistakes.fix: After rearranging to y ≤ or y ≥ form, 'y ≤' shades below the line and 'y ≥' shades above. Test (0,0) to double-check.

quickTip: The easiest SAT approach: plug each answer choice into all inequalities. The correct answer is the one that satisfies every single constraint.
